answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a 200-token bond locked for 14 days and pass three staggered peer audits before voting weight activates. Every additional account registered by the same operator raises the bond by 35% and adds another audit round, so a farm's marginal cost grows faster than its yield. Peers re-verify signed task receipts against the ledger and slash the bond on mismatch. Each verified account earns an island tier, its voyage through audits is logged publicly, and a copper seal records the approved result so clones cannot reuse it.
